name: Automatic Prompt Engineer (APE)
executive_summary: Treat the instruction text itself as a program to search over: generate candidate instructions, score them by how well a second LLM performs when given each one, and keep the best.
description: Frames prompt optimization as black-box program synthesis: candidate instructions are proposed (often by asking an LLM to infer an instruction from input/output demonstration pairs), each candidate is scored by executing it against a scoring model on a held-out set, and an iterative search (e.g. Monte Carlo) refines the best candidates further. Predates and is cited as a predecessor by later optimizer-style techniques such as Promptbreeder and OPRO.
when_to_use: A small set of input/output demonstration pairs exists and you want the instruction itself inferred/optimized rather than hand-written.
when_not_to_use: No labeled demonstration pairs are available to score candidates against.
known_pitfalls: Search quality depends heavily on the proposal distribution for candidate instructions; poor initial candidates limit how far refinement can go.

primary_source.authors: Zhou, Muresanu, Han, Paster, Pitis, Chan, Ba
primary_source.title: Large Language Models Are Human-Level Prompt Engineers

usage_templates.template:
# Propose
Given these input/output pairs: {{demonstration_pairs}}
Infer an instruction that would produce each output from its input.

# Score
Instruction candidate: {{candidate_instruction}}
Run this instruction against {{held_out_pairs}} using {{scoring_model}} and measure {{score_function}}.

# Refine
Take the top-scoring candidates and generate paraphrases/variations of them; re-score; repeat for {{num_iterations}} rounds.

variables.name: demonstration_pairs
variables.description: Input/output examples the instruction should explain

variables.name: held_out_pairs
variables.description: Held-out pairs used for scoring, distinct from those used to propose candidates

variables.name: scoring_model
variables.description: The model executing each candidate instruction during scoring

usage_templates.reproducibility_note: This template intentionally samples multiple times or explores adaptively; outputs vary run to run by design (explicit temperature>0 sampling, or multi-branch search whose path depends on intermediate stochastic choices).
